{{Quote|Deep in the lower, forgotten levels, in the oldest subbasements of ancient buildings, an entire shadowy culture has developed. Coruscant's underworld is dank and oppressive, never seeing the sun or the night sky because of the looming shadows of kilometer-high buildings. Low-flying shuttles traveling near ground level must fly with all their running lights on and weapons powered up. Otherwise, the underworld is never traveled alone.|[[Pollux Hax/Legends|Pollux Hax]]|<ref name="TISWU">''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''</ref>}}
The '''Coruscant Underworld''', '''lower levels''', '''undercity''', '''underground''', '''underlevels''', or '''Lower Coruscant''' were the lowest regions of the [[City/Legends|city]]-[[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], laid with a mixture of ancient and forgotten ruins from the planet's prehistory along with modern-looking, crime-ridden venues and clubs. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], a massive [[Underworld portal/Legends|ventilation shaft]] offered access to the heart of the underworld.

Different regions and levels ranged from the merely seedy (such as the [[Uscru Entertainment District/Legends|Uscru Entertainment District]] and [[Level 1313/Legends|1313]]), progressively worsening as one descended, to areas of unending darkness populated solely by hypertrophied vermin and [[Cthon/Legends|zombie-like devolved humanoids]]. The underworld's streets were riddled with thugs, and the walls and streets were home to all manner of strange creatures.

Most of the underworld rested more than a kilometer below the urban surface and city platforms. It was beneath some of the greatest skyscrapers in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] and other closely spaced spectacular buildings of Coruscant where few rays of light filtered through to the gloomy underworld.

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|There's no order, no civilization here. There's no health care for beings trying to eke out an existence. There's no stopping the sale of illegal drugs, or halting illicit activities, or investigations of murders here. No interference with zap gangs, or protection from Cthons. Violent deaths are an everyday occurrence, and the bodies are looted before they become food for Ferals. This is a dark place, a frightening place, and it's just easier to forget about it since we are not forced to see it every day.|[[Madhi Vaandt]]|<ref name="Allies">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Allies]]''</ref>}}
Lying hundreds of stories below the skyscraper pinnacles, Coruscant's urban canyon floors never saw the light of day.<ref name="TISWU" /> Due to its enclosure by larger buildings, air was trapped in the lower levels, creating a micro-climate of which there were at least three layers. Trapped moisture contributed to rainstorms and convective wind patterns within the canyon floors.<ref name="TISWU" /> A realm of artificial illumination, the lower levels of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] largest city were the only affordable areas for many of the planet's citizens.<ref name="CATCW">''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]''</ref> Rumbling with machines that served the elite above, its streets haunted by exploiters and thugs, and its walls riddled with vermin, Coruscant's underworld toughened the strong and consumed the weak.<ref name="CATCW" /> Coruscant's underlevels harbored a larger population than many star sectors, leaving millions beyond the protection of the world's security force.<ref name="CATCW" /> Local neighborhoods were at the mercy of hired thugs and extortionists. The toughest faces sometimes belonged to vigilantes, who chose to defend the people on their own land from criminals.<ref name="CATCW" />

Garbage was compressed into thick blocks and stored in the deeper levels of the underworld. Much machinery that satisfied the needs of the well-to-do surface dwellers was also kept in the depths of the underlevels, so there was a constant sense of motion and unrest.<ref name="AOTC:TVD">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> Artificial lighting barely brightened the dark and sorrowful levels. The underlevels were home to various mutant species including the [[Cthon/Legends|cthon]], [[Coruscani ogre]], [[Duracrete slug/Legends|duracrete slugs]], [[hive rat]]s, [[shadow barnacle]]s, [[conduit worm]], [[Taozin/Legends|taozin]], and [[Granite slug/Legends|granite slugs]], which often posed a threat to [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings.<ref name="CATCW" />

==History==
===Pre-Republic===
Little is known of the Coruscant underlevels in the [[Pre-Republic era]]. In [[100,000 BBY/Legends|100,000 BBY]], the lowest fifty levels of the [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|ecumenopolis]] had been fully built over the entire surface.<ref name="TEGTPAM">''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]''</ref> During this period, all native non-sentient species presumably became extinct with the exception of the [[Thrantcill]] (which evolved with the new city) and the [[Hawk-bat/Legends|Hawk-bat]] (which stayed the same). Around that time, the big-brained [[Columi/Legends|Columi]] visited the world and dismissed Coruscant as a primitive failure despite the presence of the planetwide city.<ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

Over the following millennia, the lower levels became the domain of criminals and vagrants. The bottom fifty levels that made up the underworld were buried under levels of [[Duracrete/Legends|duracrete]] and buildings. Several mutant species developed around this period, including the [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] Cthon and the [[Corridor ghoul/Legends|corridor ghouls]].<ref name="CATCW" />

===Galactic Republic===
Despite the [[Galactic Constitution/Legends|formation]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] in [[25,053 BBY]], life in the underlevels was left unchanged by the new galactic government.<ref name="SWTOR">{{Holonet|allegiances|galactic-republic|The Galactic Republic}}</ref> For millennia during the [[Old Republic era]], the undercity stayed the same. During the [[Great Galactic War]], food shortages caused riots in the underlevels.<ref name="Timeline 2: The Mandalorian Blockade is Broken">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 2: The Mandalorian Blockade is Broken|int=Timeline 2: The Mandalorian Blockade is Broken}}</ref><ref name="TNEC" />

[[File:Spider_Arms_Hostel.png|thumb|left|220px|The undercity during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]]]
Seedy nightclubs, overlooked gambling corners, and trashy cantinas were actually areas of some of the higher sections of these run-down nether levels. One place as dangerous as it was popular in the underlevels was the [[Uscru Entertainment District/Legends|Uscru Entertainment District]], with such hangouts as the [[Outlander Club/Legends|Outlander Club]] and the [[Snapping Septoid/Legends|Snapping Septoid]].<ref name="ITWOSW:AOTC">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones]]''</ref>

The once-famous criminal organization [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] had many allies working in the Coruscant underworld, including District Mayor [[Acros-Krik]].<ref name="TCSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> The lowest levels of the underworld had such an unbelievable crime rate that many areas were locked down by order of the government. These poor communities of desperate beggars and violent people were isolated from the rest of society by enormous, impenetrable blast doors.<ref name="TPMvideogame">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]</ref>

[[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] and her head of security, [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Quarsh Panaka/Legends|Quarsh Panaka]], got to see the underworld firsthand when she was taken hostage by mercenaries during her visit to Coruscant. Panaka was given access to one of the locked-down communities where the Queen had been taken by holding the door operator, an intellectual government agent, at gunpoint. Once rescuing Queen Amidala and killing much scum and hostiles, Panaka reopened the verbally accessible blast doors by giving the passcode phrase "Coruscant has lovely sunsets."<ref name="TPMvideogame" />

[[File:CoruscantVos.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] is tested by [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] in the bowels of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].]]
Lower-class immigrants who came to Coruscant, expecting to be living in the prosperity of the "surface life," were gradually sunken into the subterranean realms. Self-made neighborhood lookouts would often gain some small territory over their group of companions and lessers (if lower ranks could at all be possible), thus occasionally creating a tight-knit and durable community who might have even withstood hoodlum fights and minor attacks. However, once these vigilantes acquired weapons to protect their turf or began engaging in violence, even if in self-defense, there was a great chance their strengthening community would collapse to eventual criminal influences.

In [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]], [[Ashaar Khorda]] and his associates attempted to euthanize the entire planet, including the underworld, with the [[Infant of Shaa]]. The destruction of the galactic capital was hoped to be followed by the destruction of the Galactic Republic. However, their attempts to use the infant were thwarted by [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]], [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] and [[Yarael Poof/Legends|Yarael Poof]]. This resulted in the deaths of Ashaar, all his comrades, and Yarael.<ref name="SW:JF">[[Star Wars: Jango Fett (one-shot)|''Star Wars: Jango Fett'']]</ref>

===Imperial Era===
{{Quote|It should take the harbormaster down there several minutes after we dock to figure out the truth. By that time we need to be well on our way to the lowest levels of the underworld.''"<br />"''Coruscant's underworld? The lowest levels are miles down!''"<br />"''And very dangerous. Why in the world would we want to go there? We can't hide down there for long. Even if we could live in the underworld, what kind of life would that be? It's just another prison.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]|<ref name="SWM15">''[[Star Wars Missions 15: Voyage to the Underworld]]''</ref>}}
During the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] reign of the galaxy that began in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], conditions in the underworld deteriorated further, and it became a refuge for [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Jedi Purge]] survivors and dissidents.<ref name="EA:R">''[[Evasive Action: Recruitment]]''</ref> As a result of all space traffic to Coruscant being tightly controlled by the Empire and the harsh cruelty of the ruling Imperials, many criminals fled to the underworld.<ref name="TISWU" /> They ranged from bureaucrats who had made serious mistakes in their work, to diplomats from worlds punished by the Empire, to even clumsy personal servants and slaves from the [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Imperial Palace]].<ref name="TISWU" /> Thus, an entirely shadowy culture developed in the lower levels since the fugitives were forced to remain there for all their lives. These fugitives survived by revamping some of the abandoned underbasement rooms, tapping into electrical conduits, and stealing energy from the city world's power grid, while surviving upon scraps and the fungus found in these lower levels.<ref name="TISWU" />

[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] was once forced to descend to the very planetary surface, an experience he found so harrowing he vowed never to do it again, making the same vow for the surface of [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]. Also, at some time prior to the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the Emperor had the [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] ''[[Lusankya/Legends|Lusankya]]'' constructed and hidden beneath the lower levels of the planetwide city. The ''Lusankya'' became the private prison and secret headquarters of the [[Director of Imperial Intelligence|Director]] of [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]] [[Ysanne Isard]], who used it to imprison key [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] prisoners.<ref name="TEC">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref>

===New Republic===
[[File:LukeSkywalkerProfessionalExterminator-SOTETC.jpg|thumb|right|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] fighting a [[Dianoga/Legends|dianoga]] in the sewers below [[Xizor's Palace]]]]
Even after the capture of Coruscant from the Empire by the more benevolent New Republic in [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]], life in the lower levels continued as it had for millennia.<ref name="YJK:TLO">''[[Young Jedi Knights: The Lost Ones]]''</ref> After one of her captives, [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]], escaped, [[Ysanne Isard]] had the crew of the ''Lusankya'' break the immense vessel free of the planet. While leaving Coruscant, the ''Lusankya'' devastated 100 square miles (259&nbsp;km&sup2;) of the planet surface, killing millions instantly and presumably damaging a large area of the lower levels.<ref name="TEC" /> The ''Lusankya'' blasted its way through the two planetary shield levels, pausing to exchange fire with an orbiting [[Golan space defense platform]], before jettisoning the lift cradle and departing the [[Coruscant system/Legends|Coruscant system]].<ref name="TEC" />

In [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]], the [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Imperial Inner Circle]] launched an attack on Coruscant and other key worlds, having being encouraged by [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn's]] [[Thrawn campaign|devastating campaign]] throughout the New Republic. The combined Imperial armada bombarded Coruscant's energy shield from orbit, extensively damaging the heavily populated cityscape below, turning much of the planet into a battlefield and forcing [[Chief of State (New Republic)/Legends|Chief of State]] [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] to order a general evacuation of the entire population of the capital.<ref name="TEC" />

However, after Coruscant had been retaken, the Council decided that it was time to elect a new [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]]. The various [[Admiral/Legends|admirals]], [[General/Legends|generals]], [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]], [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitorius]], [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|COMPNOR]] and [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] officials disagreed, and an armed [[Imperial Civil War|conflict]] soon broke out amongst the various Imperial factions on Coruscant. The city planet was devastated during the conflict, with much of the planetwide metropolis devastated by the fighting, resulting in the deaths of billions.<ref name="TEC" />

After Palpatine's final death in [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]] at the [[Battle of Onderon (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Onderon]], the New Republic reoccupied the planet and used [[EVS Construction Droid]]s to clear the rubble and create new gleaming, skyscrapers.<ref name="TJAS">''[[The Jedi Academy Sourcebook]]''</ref> However, much of Coruscant's population had fled as result of the fighting and the planet's population during the [[New Republic era]] may have been lower. Thus, many of [[Galactic City/Legends|New Republic City's]] midlevel apartments were unoccupied, but still serviceable.<ref name="YJK:TLO" /> However, the shadowy lower levels remained unaffected by the reconstruction program and would still remain the haunt of various crime syndicates, most notably the [[Lost Ones]]. Many still struggled to survive in the lower forty or fifty levels.<ref name="YJK:TLO" />

In [[23 ABY/Legends|23 ABY]], the [[Second Imperium]] sent three [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]] named [[Tamith Kai]], [[Garowyn]], and [[Vilas]] to infiltrate the lower levels and recruit more followers for their cause including the street gang [[Lost Ones]] and [[Zekk]]. Those discovered to be Force-sensitive became [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] while others became [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] and TIE pilots.<ref name="YJK:TLO" />

===Yuuzhan'tar===
The underworld persisted through the years of [[Yuuzhan Vong]] domination, but gained some new inhabitants. When the Yuuzhan Vong [[Battle of Coruscant (Yuuzhan Vong War)|conquered]] and [[Terraforming/Legends|vongformed]] Coruscant into [[Coruscant/Legends#Yuuzhan'tar|Yuuzhan'tar]] in [[27 ABY/Legends|27 ABY]], many [[Coruscanti/Legends|Coruscanti]] fled into the underworld to escape the Yuuzhan Vong.<ref name="Traitor">''[[The New Jedi Order: Traitor]]''</ref> It was during this event the [[Yuuzhan Vong empire]] was formed, since they had claimed the galactic capital. Soon, however, the tunnels became the home of the outcasts of the Yuuzhan Vong&mdash;the [[Shamed Ones]].<ref name="TNEC" /> Fleeing torment and persecution, many Shamed Ones fled to the underworld to find honor of their own. It was also down here that [[Nom Anor]] took the guise of [[Nom Anor|Yu'shaa]], and began molding the [[Jeedai heresy|''Jeedai'' heresy]] into a true threat to the [[Elite (Yuuzhan Vong)|Elite]].<ref name="TNEC" />

The lower levels were also the domain of various life forms brought in by the Yuuzhan Vong from their [[Yuuzhan Vong galaxy|home galaxy]].<ref name="Traitor" /> In [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]] Coruscant was [[Battle of Yuuzhan'tar|liberated]] by the Galactic Alliance from Yuuzhan Vong occupation,<ref name="TUF">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force]]''</ref> but the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] world of [[Denon/Legends|Denon]] was the temporary capital of the galaxy; during that time, the surface world was reconstructed by the [[Reconstruction Authority]], but the lower levels remained largely untouched.<ref name="DNI:TJK">''[[Dark Nest I: The Joiner King]]''</ref>

===Galactic Alliance===
{{Quote|I'm coming to you live from one of the dark, dirty secrets of Coruscant&mdash;a place known variously as Lower Coruscant, the Coruscant Underworld, Undercity, or the Coruscant Underlevel. Oh, its origins are no secret. This is an ancient place, filled with ruins and stories. And recently, it was given a new name&mdash;Yuuzhan'tar. While the rest of Coruscant has been reclaimed since the end of the war, this part of the planet never fully recovered. Above me are towering buildings. Civilization. Order. Order the Galactic Alliance has established over the years. But in the midst of all the rebuilding, all the recovery, all the positive steps the GA has taken&hellip; this place has been forgotten.|[[Madhi Vaandt]]|<ref name="Allies" />}}
[[File:Underworld.jpg|thumb|left|240px|The ominous underlevels of Coruscant]]
Between [[30 ABY/Legends|30 ABY]] and [[44 ABY]], the Coruscant underlevels were left untouched by the new galactic government due to the reconstruction efforts, along with simply keeping order in the greater galaxy following the end of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] in [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]]. As late as 44 ABY, the underlevels were still overrun with exotic wildlife introduced by the Yuuzhan Vong and criminals who had survived the Fall of Coruscant. This was due to the Galactic Alliance being preoccupied with the chaos after the end of [[Second Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="Apocalypse">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]''</ref>

The underlevels still existed as late as [[137 ABY]], with one notable resident being the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] crimelady [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Jool]] who owned [[Rik's Cantina/Legends|Rik's Cantina]]. This cantina appeared to be on the lowest level of the lowest fifty levels of Coruscant.<ref name="SWL0">[[Star Wars: Legacy (2006) 0|''Star Wars: Legacy'' (2006) 0]]</ref> Following the failed [[Ossus Project]] and the [[Sith–Imperial War]], the underlevels became home to a large population of [[Vongspawn]]&mdash;sentients infected by the [[Vongspawn virus]].<ref name="SWLCOFTD">[[Legacy (2006) 14|''Legacy'' (2006) 14]]</ref>
